sample.title: Two Weeks in Mexico: The BEST Yucatan Road Trip Itinerary
sample.summary: Kate McCulley's two-week Yucatan road trip itinerary skips Cancun, Playa del Carmen and Tulum in favor of Isla Holbox, colonial Valladolid, Rio Lagartos, Merida with cenote and ruin day trips, and the Lake of Seven Colors at Bacalar. It is a full day-by-day plan with named hotel, restaurant and activity recommendations at each stop, based on her winter living in Merida and years of trips through the peninsula.

items.name: Cancun to Holbox transfer
items.details: Pick up rental car at Cancun Airport, drive 2 hours to Chiquila. Park car (100 pesos / $5 per 24h). Ferry to Isla Holbox every half hour, ~200 pesos ($10) adult.

items.name: Ser Casasandra
items.details: Recommended luxury stay on Holbox; she stayed here on her first trip. Beachfront area, pool, romantic room design, outstanding food.

items.name: Hotel Para Ti
items.details: Mid-range adults-only hotel a few blocks from town; great pool, bohemian decor; she stayed here on second trip.

items.name: Hotelito Villas Holbox
items.details: Budget hostel in the center of town; rooms small and basic but clean.

items.name: Tribu
items.details: Hostel option on Holbox; can get loud at night.

items.name: Cabo Catoche boat trip
items.details: Boat trip from Holbox to this inlet with the clearest, most beautiful water; she calls it a must. A Viator tour (snorkeling and/or fishing) is linked.

items.name: Three-island boat trip
items.details: Popular boat trip to Bird Island, uninhabited Pasion Island (sandbar walk), and Cenote Yalahau on the mainland.

items.name: Swim with whale sharks
items.details: Available June through September; peak season July and August. Called one of the coolest activities in Mexico.

items.name: Zomay
items.details: Popular sunset spot on Holbox for cocktails at sunset.

items.name: La Sardina Enamorada
items.details: Recommended breakfast stop on the mainland in Chiquila before driving on.

items.name: Drive to Valladolid
items.details: Ferry back to Chiquila, pick up car, drive just over 2 hours to Valladolid, crossing from Quintana Roo into Yucatan state (1 hour time change).

items.name: Le Muuch Hotel
items.details: Luxury pick in Valladolid; described as possibly the most beautiful property in town with chic colorful rooms, outdoor hammocks and pool.

items.name: Casa Tia Micha
items.details: Mid-range property in Valladolid that feels luxurious: classy stone bathtubs, elegant carved wood furniture, well priced and central.

items.name: Hotel Zazil-Maj
items.details: Budget hotel in Valladolid; simple but clean, recently renovated, a few blocks from Cenote Zaci.

items.name: Chichen Itza
items.details: Head to the ruins first thing in the morning; opens 8:00 AM, 45 minutes from Valladolid. Go early to beat crowds; avoid Sundays (free admission for Mexicans = very crowded). UNESCO World Heritage Site, Temple of Kukulkan.

items.name: Cenote Zaci
items.details: Cenote right in downtown Valladolid with waterfalls; one of the deepest cenotes in the region; recently reopened after renovations.

items.name: Hacienda San Lorenzo Oxman cenote
items.details: Her favorite cenote in the region: visually spectacular, large, not too touristed, lovely grounds, surprisingly good food. Alternative: Cenote Ik-Kil (similar look, more crowded).

items.name: Wabi Gelato
items.details: Gelato cafe in Valladolid; hard-to-find good gelato in Mexico, limited but inventive flavors (she loved the rosemary).

items.name: ConKafecito
items.details: Cafe on Calzada de los Frailes; she had a great pay de limon (lemon pie) here.

items.name: Days 6-14 route outline (Rio Lagartos, Merida, Bacalar)
items.details: Remaining route per her day-by-day plan: Day 6 Valladolid to Rio Lagartos; Day 7 to Merida via Izamal; Days 8-10 Merida and day trips (Uxmal, Celestun, Izamal, Campeche); Day 11 Merida to Bacalar (Lake of Seven Colors); Days 12-13 Bacalar; Day 14 Bacalar back to Cancun Airport. Notable: this itinerary deliberately skips Cancun, Playa del Carmen and Tulum.

sample.title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek - Ultimate Guide and Itinerary
sample.summary: Mark Wiens's day-by-day itinerary for his 5-day Ghorepani Poon Hill trek (mid-March 2013) starting from Pokhara: Nayapul to Tikhedunga, up to Ghorepani, sunrise at Poon Hill then on to Gandruk, Gandruk to Deurali, and back to Pokhara. Includes the lodges they stayed in, meals eaten, and costs, plus prep/permit/gear guidance.

items.name: Marigold Hotel (Amrit Tours)
items.details: Mark booked everything through Marigold Hotel/Amrit Tours in Pokhara; arranged permits and a guide ($20/day, 5 days = $100). Rooms around 700 Rupees.

items.name: Taxi from Pokhara to Nayapul
items.details: Started at about 8 am; taxi cost 1,500 Nepali Rupees. Trekking time about 5-6 hours.

items.name: Green Land Restaurant
items.details: Small house restaurant lunch stop; vegetarian dal bhat for 300 Rupees, all the rice he could eat.

items.name: Tikhedunga Guest House
items.details: Double room 350 Rupees; dinner of plain rice (150), stir fried veg noodles (270), tea (50).

items.name: Hike Tikhedunga to Ghorepani
items.details: Walked straight up the mountain ~4 hours, glimpses of snow-capped Annapurna peaks; lunch of sukuti (dry buffalo) fried with onions and spices for 400 Rupees; total hiking 7-8 hours.

items.name: Dhaulagiri Lodge
items.details: Top of the village in the main square area; 300 Rupees room, 100 Rupees hot shower; dinner of vegetable fried rice (260) and milk tea (60).

items.name: Sunrise at Poon Hill summit
items.details: 5 am climb (45 minutes) to 3,210m summit for sunrise over the Annapurna range; then hiked the parallel ridge down to Gandruk; lunch of vegetarian dal bhat for 360 Rupees; total hiking 10-12 hours.

items.name: Muna Hotel
items.details: 350 Rupees per night.

items.name: Hike Gandruk to Deurali
items.details: Mostly downhill stone steps through small villages and farms; breakfast of dal baht (360 Rupees); total hiking about 10 hours.

items.name: Hotel Trekkers Inn
items.details: Room 350 Rupees; dinner of Tibet bread (140) and omelet with rice (320).

items.name: Hike Deurali to Pothana, taxi to Pokhara
items.details: About an hour to the permit check town of Pothana, then onward to the Annapurna Eco Village (1,000 Rupees/night, stayed 1 night) before catching a taxi back to Pokhara.

sample.title: 3 days in Phuket - Rainy day itinerary
sample.destination: Phuket, Thailand (Phuket Old Town, Chalong, Patong, Nai Harn)
sample.summary: A 3-day Phuket itinerary built for rainy days, planned with HipTraveler's itinerary planner, spotlighting lesser-known corners of the island. Day 1 explores Phuket Old Town's Sino-Portuguese architecture, museums and Michelin-recognised Southern Thai food. Day 2 covers a responsible elephant sanctuary, Wat Chalong temple, the island's only rum distillery and a Muay Thai boxing night. Day 3 is relaxation at Nai Harn and Kata beaches.

items.name: Sri the Shophouse Cafe
items.location: 125 Soi Soon Utis, Phuket Old Town, Thailand
items.details: Morning coffee and breakfast in a restored Sino-Portuguese shophouse with gallery and gift shop; Japanese-style cafe, breakfast snacks and sweet treats

items.name: Phuket Thai Hua Museum
items.location: 28 Krabi Rd, Phuket Old Town, Thailand
items.details: Museum of Phuket's Chinese heritage and tin-mining history, former Thai-Chinese school; short walk from the cafe. Alternative named: The Peranakan Phuket Museum (124/1 Moo 1, Sri Soonthorn, Thalang; Peranakan heritage, photo studio in traditional costumes)
items.price_hint: 200 THB (~£4.50) adults; Peranakan museum 300 THB (~£7), audio guides included

items.name: One Chun Cafe & Restaurant
items.location: 48/1 Thep Krasattri Rd, Phuket Old Town, Thailand
items.details: Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant with retro 1950s look; Southern Thai classics: gaeng poo (crab curry with rice noodles), kaeng som (tangy Southern Thai curry), Phuket-style braised pork belly. Cash only; arrive before 12:30 to beat the lunch rush. Alternative named: KOPITIAM By Wilai (Massaman curry, Hokkien Mee)

items.name: Khao Rang Viewpoint (Monkey Hill)
items.details: Afternoon panoramic views over Phuket Town; resident macaques (do not feed, keep distance, no food bags). Tunk-ka Cafe at the viewpoint for a cold beer (prices slightly inflated)
items.price_hint: Free viewpoint; local songthaew 30-40 THB or Grab taxi to get there

items.name: The Memory at ON ON Hotel
items.location: 19 Phangnga Rd, Phuket Old Town, Thailand
items.details: Historic boutique hotel dating to 1929 (former 'Un Un Hotel'); famous as the Bangkok backpacker hostel in the film 'The Beach'; Sino-Portuguese architecture, small history museum on site; near the famous night market

items.name: Naya Restaurant & Bar, Rawai
items.details: Dinner; famous for fondue; international and Thai dishes; Penang beef curry and Massaman curry praised; attentive service, excellent value

items.name: Hidden Garden Elephant Sanctuary
items.details: Morning visit to a responsible elephant sanctuary (created late 2023 by Kong and Louise Rogerson) rescuing female elephants; observation and feeding only, no riding or bathing; 35 acres of natural forest in Chalong; 4-5 hour tour incl. briefing video, banana feeding, forest walk with mahouts, and Thai buffet lunch by the mahouts' wives
items.price_hint: Tours from ~2,800 THB (~£65) incl. pickup and lunch; most expensive item on the itinerary

items.name: Wat Chalong Temple (Wat Chaiyathararam)
items.details: Phuket's largest and most important Buddhist temple (1 of 29 on the island); honours Luang Pho Chaem and Luang Pho Chuang. Dress code: cover shoulders and knees (sarongs borrowable at entrance)

items.name: The Distillery Phuket - Chalong Bay
items.details: Afternoon at the island's only rum distillery; French couple fusing French-Caribbean rum-making with Thai heritage; French copper equipment, organic cane juice rums with local ingredients (lemongrass, Thai sweet basil); guided tours, drink-making classes, tastings and signature cocktails, onsite restaurant/bar

items.name: Patong Muay Thai Boxing
items.details: Evening authentic Muay Thai boxing in Patong (Patong Boxing Stadium / Bangla Boxing Stadium); pre-fight rituals, in-house band, drinks to your seat; front-row seats recommended
items.price_hint: Ringside from 2,100 THB (~£42-47); standard 1,500 THB (~£28-35); free T-shirt memento

items.name: Nai Harn Beach
items.details: Full relaxation day at a crescent-shaped beach with pristine white sand and laid-back vibe; protected by local regulations (no jet skis, vendors or big resorts); viewpoint with swing at the south end
items.price_hint: Beachfront pad thai/fried rice 80-120 THB; bring own water and snacks

items.name: Kata Beach and Promthep Cape
items.details: Sunset beach hopping: Kata beach sunsets; Promthep Cape & Windmill Viewpoint at the southernmost tip (~30 min drive from Kata) for Andaman Sea and Nai Harn Beach views

items.name: Nai Harn Collective
items.details: Recommended stay in Rawai: forest-surrounded oasis, two quiet pool areas, onsite spa with sauna/steam/massage, onsite bar; restaurant (Thai + Indian dishes) planned; spacious comfortable rooms with some balconies; short walk to Nai Harn beach

sample.summary: Mark Wiens's hour-by-hour one-day DIY tour of Luang Prabang: sunrise at Phou Si Mountain (6 AM), morning market snacking (7 AM), khao soi breakfast (9 AM), temples (10 AM), som tam lunch (12 PM), coffee at Saffron (2 PM), sai oua sausage (4 PM), dinner decision (6:30 PM), night market stroll (8 PM), BeerLao (9 PM).

items.details: Charcoal-grilled Laos sausage from a roadside grill along Kounxoua, near Wisdom Laos Guest House.

sample.title: 3 Days in Istanbul Itinerary
sample.summary: The perfect 3 days in Istanbul: day 1 covers Sultanahmet's historic core (Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Sultanahmet Square, Basilica Cistern, Topkapi Palace) ending with a sunset Bosphorus dinner cruise; day 2 is the Grand Bazaar, Spice Bazaar, lunch at Sehzade Cag Kebap in Eminonu, Galata Bridge, Galata Tower and Istiklal Street; day 3 is a hammam plus Kadikoy, Camlica Mosque and Uskudar on the Asian side. Co-written with The Turkey Traveler.

items.name: Traditional Turkish breakfast (kahvalti)
items.details: Start with a traditional Turkish breakfast (kahvalti): cured meats, dips, cheeses, egg, breads, pastries, honey and jams.

items.name: Hagia Sophia
items.details: Oldest building in Istanbul (537 AD); free access with museum pass or 72TL at entrance. Tram stop Sultanahmet.

items.name: Blue Mosque
items.details: Sultan Ahmet Mosque with its blue ceramic tile interior; built by Sultan Ahmed I.

items.name: Sultanahmet Square
items.details: Park connecting the two mosques; see the Obelisk of Theodosius and Ottoman fountains. Try dondurma (Turkish ice cream) here.

items.name: Basilica Cistern
items.details: Underground reservoir built 532 AD by Emperor Justinian; 336 columns. Cost 72 TL.

items.name: Topkapi Palace
items.details: Ottoman sultans' palace/museum with Harem; famous tiling and treasury exhibits.

items.name: Sunset Bosphorus dinner cruise
items.details: Evening cruise from the Golden Horn covering the Bosphorus Strait between Europe and Asia; they recommend a 2.5-hour luxury dinner cruise with Turkish food (meze, raki) and Whirling Dervishes.

items.name: Grand Bazaar
items.details: One of the oldest and largest covered markets in the world: 61 streets, 4000+ shops; try a Turkish rug, lantern or nazar amulet, and relax in a tea shop with çay.

items.name: Spice Bazaar
items.details: 17th-century L-shaped market overwhelmed by the smell of spices; great place to buy Turkish tea.

items.name: Sehzade Cag Kebap
items.details: Their favorite restaurant in Eminonu for lamb sis kebap that melts in the mouth; affordable local flavors.

items.name: Galata Bridge
items.details: Walk across the 490m Galata Bridge over the Golden Horn, lined with local fishermen.

items.name: Galata Tower
items.details: Most famous attraction in modern Istanbul, in the Beyoglu district; built 1348.

items.name: Istiklal Street and Taksim
items.details: Evening on the modern city's famous shopping and nightlife street with Taksim Square.

items.name: Turkish bath (Hammam)
items.details: Morning Turkish bath on the final day.

items.name: Kadikoy
items.details: Food and cafe district on the Asian side.

items.name: Camlica Mosque and Uskudar
items.details: Mosque with Maiden's Tower area views in Uskudar.

items.details: 7-day card with skip-the-line tickets to top attractions, 10 public transport rides, and vouchers for Hagia Sophia, Basilica Cistern, Topkapi Palace and the Bosphorus cruise.

items.details: Dinner day 1: oyster / small plates spot; raw bar, truffle fries, beef carpaccio, oysters Rockefeller, redfish, steak.

items.details: Free synchronized water, light and music show nightly 6-9pm outside Malco Renaissance Cinema Grill.

items.details: Dinner day 2: Ridgeland institution since 1989. Book ahead, especially when the legislature is in session.
